stem:
Tanya buys apples grown in a nearby orchard instead of apples trucked from far away.

Why can eating more local food help?

options.text: Any food labelled local always has fewer food miles, even if it went through a distant warehouse.
Shorter producer-to-consumer travel means fewer food miles, which can cut cost and pollution.
Putting the same distant apples on sale reduces their food miles even if the delivery route is unchanged.
Food miles stop at the shop, so carrying food home does not count.

teacher.key_rationale: Food miles are the full distance from producer to consumer; choosing nearby food shortens that path and can lower cost and pollution. Labels, sale prices, and stopping the count at the shop do not redefine the travel distance.
